items.title: The preamble of §15.1: $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$

book.label: §15.1, preamble, p. 683 (2017: §15.1)
book.statement: $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$ is the set of finite formal sums with coefficients in $\mathbb Q^+$ of sc-Fredholm operators $T_xX \to W_x$, for smooth $x$; a morphism $\varphi$ acts by $\varphi_*$.

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.GrF x := (T_xX →ₗ[ℝ] W_x) →₀ ℚ≥0` for $x \in X_1$, with $W_x = P^{-1}(x)$ and $T_xX$ the project's tangent fibre; the chart version `Linearization15.GrFModel`.

diff: Formal sums are finitely supported functions, defined at all level-1 points. That the summands are sc-Fredholm is not part of the type (gap G.145); $\varphi_*$ and $\mathrm{GrF}(X)$ as a category are not built (gap G.144).

items.title: Theorem 15.1.1 (2017: 15.1), the linearization $T(f,\Lambda)$ is well defined

book.label: §15.1, Theorem 15.1.1, pp. 684–687 (2017: Theorem 15.1)
book.statement: For an sc-Fredholm section $f$ and an sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda$ there is a unique section functor $T(f,\Lambda)$ of $\mathrm{GrF}(X) \to X_\infty$ with (1) $T(f,\Lambda)(x) = 0$ off $\mathrm{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$ and (2) $T(f,\Lambda)(y) = \sum_{f(y) = s_i(y)} \sigma_i (f - s_i)'(y)$ for any local sc⁺-section structure.

lean.statement: `theorem_15_1_1_intrinsic`: for `A.E.IsScFredholmSectionFunctor f`, two local section structures `IsLocalRepOn A Λ O s σ`, `IsLocalRepOn A Λ O′ t τ` on open sets and compatible charts with domains inside them, `linSumIntr c hx f s σ = linSumIntr c′ hx′ f t τ` at every $x \in X_1$ in both charts ($\sum_{f(x) = s_i(x)} \sigma_i\,\Phi_x^{-1} \circ D((\hat f - \hat s_i) \circ r)(\varphi x) \circ T\varphi$ in $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$). Chart form `theorem_15_1_1`, model form `theorem_15_1_1_model`. The value: `linearization_eq` (property (2) for any data), `nonempty_localLinData`; property (1): `linearization_eq_zero`.

diff: The well-definedness, the substance of the proof, is proved in a stronger form: at all level-1 points, for $\Lambda$ not necessarily a functor, using only sc-smoothness of $f$. Narrower because the functor property $T(f,\Lambda)(t\varphi) = \varphi_* T(f,\Lambda)(s\varphi)$ (gap G.144) and the sc-Fredholm property of the summands (gap G.145) are not formalized.

Readings (Findings, Chapter 15, items 1, 2): (a) the separation argument runs in the level-1 topology, and the "weak topology" of the limit of derivatives is read as pointwise convergence on $E_0$ (the derivatives $D(g \circ r)$ of an sc¹ map are continuous only from level 1); (b) in the final display, presumably the sum is over $\{i : f(0) = s_i(0)\}$, since $f(0) = s_i(0)$ need not hold for all $i$; the proof compares the formal sums of pairs $(s_i(r(y)), D((f - s_i) \circ r)(y))$. "Without loss of generality $X = O$" is the chart change `toIntr_chart_independent`.

items.title: Remark 15.1.2 (2017: 15.1), (1) follows from (2)

book.label: §15.1, Remark 15.1.2, p. 684 (2017: Remark 15.1)
book.statement: $(f - s_i)'(y)$ is not defined unless $f(y) = s_i(y)$, but then it is not counted; with the empty sum $0$, (1) follows from (2).

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.linearization_eq_zero`: if $\Lambda(f(x)) = 0$ then `linearization f Λ x = 0`; chart forms `remark_15_1_2`, `remark_15_1_2_model`; with positive weights an operator lies in the support iff some $i$ with $s_i(y) = f(y)$ produces it (`mem_support_linSumModel_iff`).

diff: In Lean $(f - s_i)'$ is defined for every $i$ and the sum is filtered by $s_i(y) = f(y)$; (1) is derived from positivity of the weights and the count formula.

items.title: Proposition 15.1.3 (2017: 15.1), separating sequences

book.label: §15.1, Proposition 15.1.3, p. 684 (2017: Proposition 15.1)
book.statement: In the local model there are $x_k \to 0$ with $x_k \ne 0$ and a partition $I = I_1 \sqcup \dots \sqcup I_p$ such that $s_i(x_k) = s_{i'}(x_k)$ iff $i, i'$ lie in the same $I_e$, and then $s_i = s_{i'}$ near $x_k$.

lean.statement: `Linearization15.proposition_15_1_3_hyp`: in a first countable $T_1$ space $Z$, for finitely many maps continuous on an open $V \ni x_0$ with values in a Hausdorff space, and **$x_0$ not isolated** (`(𝓝[≠] x₀).NeBot`): $x_k \in V$, $x_k \ne x_0$, $x_k \to x_0$, and one partition $e : I \to \mathrm{Fin}\,p$ with `IsSeparatedAt s e (x k)` for all $k$. At an isolated point no such sequence exists: `not_proposition_15_1_3_of_isolated`, `not_proposition_15_1_3_point` (a one-point model). Witness: `proposition_15_1_3_hyp_witness` ($\mathbb R$ at 0).

diff: Hidden hypotheses: $x_0$ is not isolated; witness `proposition_15_1_3_hyp_witness`.

At an isolated point of the local model (for instance a zero-dimensional $X$) a sequence $x_k \ne 0$, $x_k \to 0$ cannot exist, so the proposition does not hold as we read it there (`not_proposition_15_1_3_of_isolated`); a degenerate case (Findings, Chapter 15, item 3). Theorem 15.1.1 is unaffected: its core lemma handles isolated points through locality. Otherwise the statement is more general: topological, with no sc-structure.

items.title: Lemma 15.1.4 (2017: 15.1), finite closed covers of a ball

book.label: §15.1, Lemma 15.1.4, p. 685 (2017: Lemma 15.1)
book.statement: If a ball $B_\varepsilon(y)$ in $\mathcal O$ (metric of $E_0$) is a finite union of sets closed in the ball, one of them has nonempty interior.

lean.statement: `Linearization15.lemma_15_1_4`, in any pseudo-metric space: for finitely many relatively closed $A_i$ with $\bigcup A_i = B_\varepsilon(y)$, some $A_i$ has nonempty interior; topological core `exists_nonempty_interior_of_finite_closed_cover`.

diff: The proof is by induction on the index set instead of moving $z$ step by step; it is applied on the level-1 topology (reading (a) of V15.2).

items.title: Lemma 15.1.5 (2017: 15.2), local dichotomy of finitely many sections

book.label: §15.1, Lemma 15.1.5, p. 685 (2017: Lemma 15.2)
book.statement: For $y$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ there are $z$ with $d(z,y) < \varepsilon$, $\delta > 0$ and a partition $I_1, \dots, I_p$ with $B_\delta(z) \subset B_\varepsilon(y)$, $s_i = s_{i'}$ on $B_\delta(z)$ within one piece and $s_i \ne s_j$ pointwise on $B_\delta(z)$ across pieces.

lean.statement: `Linearization15.lemma_15_1_5`: in a pseudo-metric space, for finitely many maps continuous on $B_\varepsilon(y)$ into a Hausdorff space, exactly these conclusions, the partition a surjection $e : I \to \mathrm{Fin}\,p$; topological form `exists_isOpen_dichotomy`.

diff: The maps need only be continuous with values in a Hausdorff space; the sections need not be sc⁺.

items.title: Remark 15.1.6, modifying the sequence

book.label: §15.1, Remark 15.1.6, p. 686 (not in the 2017 text)
book.statement: One can start from any sequence $x'_k \to 0$, modify it slightly to $x''_k$ and take a subsequence with the properties of Proposition 15.1.3; slight modifications keep the properties.

lean.statement: `Linearization15.remark_15_1_6` (metric space): from $x'_k \to x_0$ in $V$, points $x''_k \in V$ with $d(x'_k, x''_k) < 1/(k+1)$, $x''_k \to x_0$, a subsequence and a partition with `IsSeparatedAt` along it. `IsSeparatedAt.eventually`: separation at $z$ persists near $z$.

diff: "Slightly" is $d < 1/(k+1)$ in the first part and "eventually near $z$" in the second.

book.label: §15.1, Definition 15.1.7, p. 687 (2017: Definition 15.1)
book.statement: $T(f,\Lambda)$ is the linearization of $\Lambda \circ f$ on $\mathrm{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$, and $T(f,\Lambda)(x)$ the linearization at $x$.

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.linearization f Λ x : GrF x` for $x \in X_1$, the formal sum of some `LocalLinData A Λ x` (a local section structure and a chart around $x$ inside it), $0$ if there is none; independent of the choice (`linearization_eq`), data exist (`nonempty_localLinData`), $0$ off the support (`linearization_eq_zero`). Chart reading `linearizationIn`.

notFormalized.title: Theorem 15.1.1, the functor property of $T(f,\Lambda)$
notFormalized.label: §15.1, Theorem 15.1.1, p. 684 (2017: Theorem 15.1)
notFormalized.book: For a morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ between smooth points, $T(f,\Lambda)(y) = \varphi_* T(f,\Lambda)(x)$, where $\varphi_*$ maps $\sum \sigma_i L_i$ to $\sum \sigma_i\,\mu(\varphi,\cdot) \circ L_i \circ T\varphi^{-1}$.
notFormalized.instead: $T(f,\Lambda)(x)$ is defined and well defined at every $x \in X_1$ (`SBLocalization.linearization`, `linearization_eq`; V15.2, V15.8), and the linear tangent map of a morphism exists (`EpGroupoid.tangentMorCLM`). Missing: the action $\varphi_*$ on `GrF`, the transport of a local section structure along $t \circ s^{-1}$ near $\varphi$, and the chain rule for `linAt` along it. Estimate 300–500 lines.

notFormalized.title: §15.1 and Theorem 15.1.1 (2): the summands of $T(f,\Lambda)(x)$ are sc-Fredholm
notFormalized.label: §15.1, preamble and Theorem 15.1.1 (2), pp. 683–684 (2017: §15.1, Theorem 15.1)
notFormalized.book: Each $(f - s_i)'(x)$ with $f(x) = s_i(x)$ is an sc-Fredholm operator $T_xX \to W_x$, so $T(f,\Lambda)(x) \in \mathrm{GrF}(x)$.
notFormalized.instead: `SBLocalization.GrF x` allows all linear maps, and `toIntr` is the intrinsic $(f - s_i)'(x)$ (V15.1, V15.2). Missing: $f - s_i$ is sc-Fredholm near $x$ (an sc⁺-perturbation), its linearization at a zero is sc-Fredholm (identifying `linAt` with the sc-Fredholm germ linearization), and a subtype of `GrF` with Fredholm summands. Estimate 200–400 lines.
